questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Interesting and challenging courses and research programmes. Nature and fresh air.

How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Quite difficult. I lived in a Burschenschaft which was the only thing I could find.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: In Heidelberg there are many student-associations who are subletting rooms but they demand participation in many activities which might not suit everyone. Housing is difficult to find if you do it on your own.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Kind of difficult and it is not certain that you will get the courses you apply for.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You register online on the Heico website and for some courses you have to write the professor directly, and it is important to register the courses well in advance.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Help came from online guides and employees.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was partially successfull and I got 80% of the courses i wanted to get.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do it well in advance and write the course leaders if you are in doubt about the process.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Most of my courses were on MA level which suited me well but generally the BA courses are on a higher level compared to University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was overall similar but Heidelberg had more presentations and more in depth teaching.

What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Rowing I think. I did a bit of fencing at my fraternity but that had nothing to do with host institution.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hiking and maybe swimming in the Neckar. The river is a bit dirty but you can swim there. I did a lot of walking in the surrounding mountais and also very often went to Frankfurt to go partying and see art exhibitions.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
I recommend perhaps going to Paris or Berlin or Colmar or Strassbourg, it is neaby compared to Copenhagen and it feels great to go there and get out of Heidelberg once in a while like a european cosmopolitan. 
Go maybe to Marbach to see Schillers birth place and the german museum of literature. Maybe also to Weimar. The old opera house in Frankfurt has good concerts once in a while. Theater in Heidelberg is ok, and sometime the screen good movies at Karlstor.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Yes very easy but also demanding at times. Germans can do mind their own buissiness a lot like people do in Denmark and they usually never approach you in public unless they are very drunk. There are many festivites in Heidelberg old city and therefore a lot of noise but this is also charming.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just approach people and be not afraid of exhibiting yourself and your flaws. Get their number and go for a walk go get lunch together at marstall. Enjoy solitude.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
That people look into their phones so much in public. Especially in the trains. It is horrible to be among these screens all of the time. Germans love staring at their screens whenever they go outside their door. 
There are a lot of tourist in Heidelberg and they are very indifferent to your presence which sometimes feels a bit estranging. they constantly take photos of the bride and the castle.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I appreciate that the germans are ready for a debate about politics or history. You can always get a long discussion about opportunism for instance and they will listen to you carefully if you are polite.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: That Heidelberg can offer you a lot of knowledge and new strategies to approach your research academic career. You can make friends there that you can have for a long time afterwards. Strong bonds are likely to form!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university usually dont offer examples of previous exams for you to practice on. So you just gotta learn everything that they present on their powerpoints or on the blackboard. Usually this means solving the tasks they give you during the course and learning how to solve them by heart, this will make you do well at the exams.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To make new friends. To learn.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having to do my exams in Heidelberg while my semester in Copenhagen had already begund in the begining of februrary. That was kind of annoying but manageable.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I generally recomend going on exchange! Its a good idea especially if you havent lived outside Denmark before. It changes your sense of sovereignty and your life ulitmatly.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
